sessions.must_catch: Per-turn cache reads collapsed 40000 -> 50 (ratio 0.001); name the boundary and give a concrete re-cache/resume action.
Cache miss caused by a >1h idle gap (5m/1h TTL expired); recommend resuming sooner or consolidating the idle window.
A mid-session context edit invalidated the cached prefix (re-creation > 2x prior); recommend batching prefix edits.
~3 large 5m-TTL prefix re-caches after idle with near-zero reads; quantify wasted write tokens; recommend a TTL/idle mitigation.
Same as the 5m churn case for the 1h-TTL band; the larger write volume should rank it above the 5m session.
Base-seed B1 cache-read collapse lane; kept for continuity with prior H1 work — flag the collapse and name a re-cache action.

context_tokens_max ~193000 is very large per turn; recommend trimming always-loaded context / session boundaries. The engine currently MISSES this (D2 requires >=150 turns) — this session measures whether the engine under-fires vs. the Claude arm.
Nothing. Stable cache reads and small writes — neither the engine nor the Claude arm may invent a recommendation. False-positive check.
Nothing. Tiny healthy session with no signal — no recommendation. False-positive check.
>=3 NOT_FOUND tool errors on a single session should surface as a C2 finding. The co-firing D7 loop finding is a WANTED signal — repeated NOT_FOUND calls are a genuine loop.

A NOT_READ error on Edit (editing a file not previously read) should surface as C3 within the window. A co-firing D7 loop finding here is a FALSE POSITIVE — a single edit-no-read is not a loop; the engine should ideally suppress it.
5 consecutive same-file Edit failures should surface as a C4 finding. The co-firing D7 loop finding is WANTED — 5 consecutive same-file failures are a genuine loop.
>=3 identical tool+error_class repetitions should surface as a C5 error-loop finding. The co-firing D7 loop finding is WANTED — this session IS an error loop.
>=3 failed Bash commands of the same family (BASH_GIT) should surface as a C7 finding. The co-firing D7 loop finding is WANTED — repeated same-family Bash failures are a genuine loop.

Each distinct denial class (hook-block, deny-rule, user-rejected) should produce a C9 finding. A co-firing D7 loop finding here is a FALSE POSITIVE — distinct denial classes are not a repetition loop; the engine should ideally suppress it.
An MCP_CONTENT_TOO_LARGE tool error should surface as a C11 finding.
Both interrupt kinds (PURE_INTERRUPT, KILLED_NO_PROMPT) should produce separate D14 findings.
Each destructive-op class (rm-rf, git-reset-hard) should produce a separate H1 finding.
